title: Ureteroscopy
also: kidney stone removal with a scope
what: A urologist passes a thin instrument with a camera through the urethra into the bladder and ureter. There are no cuts. Most often this is how stones are broken up and removed.
why: For a stone in the ureter or kidney that will not pass on its own; sometimes for a narrowed ureter or to take a tissue sample.
duration: usually 30 to 90 minutes; a hospital stay of usually 1 to 2 days, sometimes home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will tell you what to change and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you have a fever or signs of a urinary infection now
If you or relatives had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Urine test, urine culture, blood tests, and a kidney CT or ultrasound. The clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: They will ask about your health and medicines and choose the anesthesia: general or spinal.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before and no drinks for a few hours before. The clinic will give you the exact times.

bring: Your documents and a list of medicines
Things for 1 to 2 days in hospital
steps: An IV line is put in a vein
In the operating room, the anesthesiologist gives anesthesia
The urologist passes a thin instrument through the urethra, with no cuts
The stone is broken up with a laser, and the pieces are removed
Often a thin tube called a stent is placed from the kidney to the bladder while things heal
You wake up in your room, sometimes with a catheter in your bladder
feel: Burning when peeing and a frequent urge to go
Pink urine in the first days
With a stent: a pulling feeling in your side when peeing
after: Drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
The stent is usually removed after a few days or weeks. Do not miss this date
Stone pieces may pass in your urine for a few days
The stone may be sent for testing. This helps choose ways to prevent new stones
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) or chills: see a doctor right away or call emergency services
You cannot pee: call emergency services
Severe pain in your side that does not go away with painkillers
Bright red urine or urine with clots

faq.a: No. The instrument goes in through a natural opening, the urethra.

faq.q: Why a stent, and when will it come out?
faq.a: The stent helps urine drain while the ureter heals. Your urologist will tell you when to remove it. It is important not to miss this.

reminders.text: Ureteroscopy tomorrow. Pack your things, documents, and images. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
